title: request-sketchbook-customer-mini-docket-jun-2026
content:
Purpose: quick, portable synthesis of the last two weeks of field feedback from top-tier customers and a short list of small-to-medium fixes/probes we can ship in 1–3 sprints. This is intentionally messy — rollout notes, raw quotes, hypotheses, and suggested owners. Use as a working inbox for eng/product prioritization and fast experiments.

Context snapshot (customers sampled):
- FinOps SaaS startup (Dedicated customer) — heavy multitenant traffic, very sensitive to per-token cost.
- HealthTech enterprise (Private deployment pilot) — tight compliance, wants on-prem inference with predictable p99 latency.
- Market research platform (hosted) — uses embeddings at scale, occasional degradation in quality after model swaps.

Selected raw customer snippets (verbatim-ish):
- "We saw a 2x token-cost jump overnight after a model fallback. Need a flag to force exact variant across regions." — FinOps lead
- "Our users expect sub-200ms response for short prompts. Recent canary increased p99 to ~420ms in us-west1." — SRE at HealthTech
- "Embeddings drifted; search recall dropped for fine-grained taxonomy queries after last model update." — ML lead, Research platform

Observed problem clusters + representative evidence: (quick mapping)
1) Cost surprises during automated fallbacks
   - Incidents: RDW-4321 (ticket) + multiple support threads (CS-1189).
   - Root signals: lack of per-route pinned model override when routing policy changes; fallback to larger model variant without clear billing callout.
   - Customer impact: sudden invoice increases, churn risk for cost-sensitive startups.

2) Latency regressions in short-tail prompts after canary changes
   - Evidence: tracing spikes in us-west1; p99 moved from 180ms to 420ms for <64 token payloads.
   - Hypothesis: canary rollout enabled different batching policy (larger dynamic batch windows) for seemingly identical route tags.
   - Customer impact: UX regressions, product teams disable canaries to avoid user complaints.

3) Quality drift for embeddings after model swaps
   - Evidence: user reports + automated evals show recall drop for taxonomy queries when model variant moved from embed-v1-small -> embed-v2-quant.
   - Hypothesis: quantized variant has degraded nearest-neighbor properties for sparse taxonomic distinctions; default evaluation set didn't include these corner queries.
   - Customer impact: search relevance falls, support tickets and manual rollback requests.

Quick prioritized probe list (impact / effort rough):
- P1 (High impact / Low effort): "Billing-callout on fallback" flag — add a per-route boolean: annotate fallback billing delta in API response and console, and send one-line Slack/email alert to customer admins when fallback happens. (owner: Liam Chen; eng spike 2d; ship in hotfix).
- P2 (High impact / Medium effort): "Canary batching visibility" — expose active batching policy per route in Console live view and add a telemetry field in trace payloads so customers can see changes during rollouts. (owner: Sofia Moreno; eng 1 sprint + console small UI).
- P3 (Medium impact / Medium effort): "Embedding sanity probe harness" — expand eval sets to include customer-provided taxonomy queries and run daily embedding regressions on new variants; add auto-notify if recall drops > 6%. (owner: Evan Brooks; product + applied-ml collaboration).
- P4 (Low impact / Low effort): "Short prompt fast-path" — experiment with disabling large-window batching for routes with median prompt length < 64 tokens. Feature flag controlled; measure latency delta. (owner: oncall SRE; 3d experiment).

Mini design notes / implementation constraints:
- Billing-callout on fallback: do not expose internal model names to customers (legal/contract), instead surface a delta estimate and link to policy page. Need finance sign-off on wording.
- Canary batching visibility: trace schema already includes batch_size and queue_time; Console needs a lightweight overlay that maps trace -> active config at that minute.
- Embedding harness: add a customer-provided small corpus (encrypted at rest) and run NN recall; lock KMS scope for private deployments. For hosted customers, use opt-in with data terms.

Unresolved questions / decisions needed:
- Should fallback billing deltas be retroactive (do we credit customers after the fact) or only future-notification? (ops/legal tradeoffs).
- For private deployments, can we run daily embedding regressions inside the customer's VPC or do we require snapshots exported to Redwood test infra? (security).
- What SLOs do we promise once we introduce per-route batching visibility? (need SRE input).

Suggested short-term playbook for CS+SEs:
1) Reach out to the three impacted customers with tailored notes: explain we have short probes planned (billing-callout + canary batching visibility), propose 1:1 sessions for the embedding harness opt-in.
2) Open a shared Slack channel with each customer during canary windows and add an engineer to monitor traces.
3) Offer a 30-day invoice review if fallback billing deltas exceed 10% for any month (pilot).

Next steps / owners (this doc is the living TODO):
- Liam: implement billing-callout API change + email template (deliverable: api change PR + console blurb) — ETA: 2026-06-22
- Sofia: spec Console overlay + trace mapping; coordinate with SRE to capture batch metrics — ETA: 2026-06-29
- Evan: prototype embedding harness and coordinate privacy checklist for private installs — ETA: 2026-07-05
- Asha (me): outreach plan and customer comms templates, schedule 1:1s this week.

Notes to self / quick links:
- Related support threads: CS-1189 (billing complaints), CS-1215 (latency escalation).
- Quick demo dataset for embedding probe is in shared GCS: gs://redwood-cs/dev-embed-probes/june-2026 (contact Evan for access).

Appendix (short dumps):
- Example console wording for billing-callout: "Fallback triggered to maintain latency SLO; estimated additional cost: ~0.9 tokens per request. View configuration or request a pin."
- Example Slack DM template for warm-handoff during canary: "Hi <name>, we're starting a brief canary for route <route>. Expect short blips; ping this channel if you spot p99 regressions >250ms for more than 5 minutes. Engineer oncall: <name>."

End of mini-docket. Keep this lean; I'll iterate after the first round of implementation feedback.
